findings.title: Public findMany() method removed and replaced with getBaseConditions(), breaking the service's contract
findings.body: The previous implementation exposed `findMany(findManyArgs)` which executed the query against `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized` and returned rows. This PR removes that method entirely and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment and requires the caller to manually construct and execute a raw `$queryRaw` query (as the test now does). Any production code that calls `InsightsBookingService.findMany(...)` (e.g. insights routes/UI data fetchers) will fail to compile/run after this change, since the method no longer exists. The PR description claims this is only a test update to match an already-converted implementation, but the diff shows the public API of the service itself is being changed in the same PR, which is a contract break that isn't validated against other call sites in the diff.

findings.title: Array-based ANY(...) SQL conditions for team/org scope are never executed against the real database in tests
findings.body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` build SQL like `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND (...)` where `teamIds`/`userIdsFromTeam` are JS number arrays interpolated via Prisma.sql. Passing arrays as parameters to `ANY()` in raw Postgres queries can require explicit type casts (e.g. `ANY($1::int[])`) depending on the driver/parameter binding, otherwise Postgres may fail with a parameter type inference error at execution time. The only integration test that actually executes a query via `prisma.$queryRaw` (the renamed `getBaseConditions` test) exercises the 'user' scope, which does not use `ANY()`. The 'team' and 'org' scope tests only assert structural equality of the constructed `Prisma.Sql` object and never actually run the query against the database, so a runtime failure in the ANY()-array binding for team/org scopes (explicitly called out as a risk in the PR's own review checklist) would not be caught by these tests.

findings.title: Caching behavior tests were removed even though the caching logic still exists in the service
findings.body: The previous test suite had a `describe("Caching", ...)` block verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return cached results on subsequent calls (backed by `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` fields). This PR deletes those tests entirely without replacing them, while the service implementation (`insightsBooking.ts`) still contains and relies on this same caching mechanism (fields `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions`, lines 49-50 and 83-95). Removing these tests silently drops coverage for an existing, still-present feature, so a regression in caching (e.g., accidentally rebuilding the Prisma.Sql object on each call, or caching stale/incorrect conditions) would go undetected.

findings.title: PR description scope does not match actual diff contents
findings.body: The PR description states this change only updates the integration test file to match a service implementation that was 'previously converted' to Prisma.sql, implying `insightsBooking.ts` itself was not modified by this PR. However the diff shows substantial changes to `insightsBooking.ts` (import change from `import type { Prisma }` to `import { Prisma }`, removal of `findMany`, new `getBaseConditions` method, rewritten condition-building logic). This mismatch between the stated scope and the actual change makes it harder for reviewers to know which parts of the service logic are newly introduced in this PR versus pre-existing, and increases risk that the 'HIGH RISK' authorization/SQL logic in the service itself did not receive a dedicated, scoped review.
